production.note: Calendar years, as in the Bugatti and Rimac records. CAR (November 2021) drove a pre-series car, with the first production car "scheduled for this month" and Battistas "just filling the last few build slots for 2022"; customer cars are a 2022-on run of "A maximum of 150 Battistas ... hand-assembled in Cambiano, Italy". EVKX lists MY2022-MY2025 (evkx-battista). No opened page states that production has ended. The 2019 release allocates the 150 cars "equally between the regions of North America, Europe and Middle East/Asia", so the car is sold in the US (pininfarina-reveal-2019).

body.note: Inferred: a two-door, fixed-roof electric hyper GT.

configuration.note: "Four motors, one per wheel, mean torque vectoring becomes a key performance parameter"

transmission.note: CAR's spec sheet: "Single-speed transmission, all-wheel drive"; "each axle controlled by its own single-speed gearbox".

powerHp.note: The maker's rating is given in kW: 1,400 kW x 1.34102 = 1,877 hp. Quote (Automobili Pininfarina reveal release, technical table): "Power output Up to 1,900 hp (1,400 kW)". The "1,900 hp" is metric horsepower (1,400 kW = 1,904 PS); it is converted from kW as for the Chiron and Nevera. CAR and Top Gear print the same rating as "1874bhp" / "a headline figure of 1,874bhp" (car-battista, topgear-battista), i.e. 1,900 PS converted to bhp.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: no manufacturer weight was found on any opened page. 2,200 kg x 2.20462 = 4,850 lb. Quote (CAR specification panel, Ben Barry): "2200kg (approx.), carbonfibre". Greg Kable reports the same number as a kerb weight: "under 2,200kg" (iia-battista-kable). The EVKX database lists "2302 kg (5075 lbs)" curb instead - see discrepancies.

sources.publisher: Automobili Pininfarina (press release PDF on the company's media store)
sources.title: Pininfarina Battista - the world's first pure electric luxury hyper GT revealed (4 March 2019)

discrepancies.reason: Units: the maker's "1,900 hp" is metric horsepower (PS); 1,400 kW converts to 1,877 hp; the magazines convert 1,900 PS to 1,874 bhp.
discrepancies.resolution: Stored 1,877 hp from the manufacturer's kW figure, per the guide's kW conversion (as for the Chiron and Nevera).

discrepancies.reason: Unknown. The database's 2,302 kg may be an EU homologated mass (with driver) or a later/heavier configuration; the two editorial sources with named authors both give 2,200 kg.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 2,200 kg, the figure the two named-author editorial sources agree on; kept provisional until a manufacturer figure is found.

provisionalNote: Weight (2,200 kg / 4,850 lb) is provisional: CAR's panel prints "2200kg (approx.)" and Greg Kable reports a kerb weight "under 2,200kg", while the EVKX database lists 2,302 kg; Automobili Pininfarina has published no weight on any opened page. Production years (2022-present) rest on CAR's build-slot reporting and EVKX's model-year list. An Automobili Pininfarina specification sheet, or a major-magazine panel with a labelled kerb weight, would replace the weight. Power (1,400 kW) is from the manufacturer's release.
